beats.text: Sad after sex? Even when it was good? You're not broken.
Researchers in Australia asked women, and later over twelve hundred men, about feelings right after sex.
Forty-six percent of women had felt sad, tearful or irritable afterwards at least once.
And men? Forty-one percent. One in five in the past four weeks alone.
It even happened in loving relationships, after sex that felt good.
It has a name: post-sex blues. So if it hits you, say it out loud. It's not about them.

sources: Schweitzer, O'Brien, Burri et al. (2015). Postcoital dysphoria: prevalence and psychological correlates. Sexual Medicine 3(4). Australian university women: 46% lifetime, ~5% past month. Via WBUR / ISSM.

Maczkowiack & Schweitzer (2019, online 2018). Postcoital dysphoria: prevalence and correlates among males. Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy 45(2). 1,208 men online: 41% lifetime, 20% past four weeks, 3-4% regularly. Via ISSM.
